desc: Derive the structural reduction: for a fixed center c, each neighbor v can serve as a middle (blue) vertex with exactly y kept leaf children iff deg(v)-1 >= y, contributing y+1 kept vertices; otherwise the whole branch is deleted (contributes 0). No deeper DP needed since snowflakes have exactly 3 levels and leaf children contribute exactly 1 each.

Key simplification: child-count of neighbor v relative to center c is deg(v)-1 regardless of c, so no rerooting/DFS maps are needed — the problem reduces to per-center aggregation over neighbor degrees.

Formula: kept(c) = 1 + max over y>=1 of (y+1) * #{neighbors v of c with deg(v) >= y+1}; equivalently sort neighbor degrees descending d_1..d_m and take max of d_i * i over i with d_i >= 2. Answer = N - max_c kept(c).
Verify formula on samples: Sample 1 -> kept(4)=7, answer 1 ✓; Sample 2 -> center 1 (endpoint), kept=3, answer 0 ✓; Sample 3 -> center 2 gives kept=7, answer 3 ✓.

Edge cases: star is a snowflake with x=1, y=N-2 (answer 0); any tree with N>=3 contains a path of length 2 = snowflake x=1,y=1, so a valid answer always exists; centers with no neighbor of deg>=2 contribute nothing (kept=1, never optimal).
Implement final Python solution with fast I/O (sys.stdin.buffer), adjacency lists, per-center descending sort of neighbor degrees (total O(N log N)), compute best kept, print N - best.

Verify the implementation against additional edge cases and stress-test correctness: star (answer 0), paths (P_3→0, P_4→1, P_N→N-5 for N≥5), non-maximal-y optima (neighbor degrees {5,2,2,2} correctly prefers y=1,x=4 over y=4,x=1), and a rigorous upper-bound/achievability proof replacing brute-force cross-check.
